original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can scripts/partial_swap/shared.py:SharedPointCircuit.__init__ emit the same merge/lookup DAG (same args/core/union/provenance/outputs/active/merged_additions and the same circuit_sha256) with a tighter construction loop, so full-size partial-swap builds stay fieldwise identical while certificates/partial-swap-network.json updates only the shared.py source_sha256 pin?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one measured replay bottleneck with before/after wall time and retained checks. Expertise override selected verifier-engineering after open tooling PR #2039 left SharedPointCircuit.__init__ merge/lookup construction as an explicit next question on the partial-swap producer fork, and open #2054 answered the same construction object on the canonical scripts/shared_point_circuit.py. This package ports that constructor rewrite to scripts/partial_swap/shared.py stacked on the #2039 tip so verify digests are not regresssed. Profiling named the per-common-point merge loop (repeated sorted(active), per-node generator unpacks, repeated attribute lookups) as the construction bottleneck; ExclusionCircuit/DisjointTensor support masks (#2001) stay untouched.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review throughput: partial-swap producers, skip-strip graphs and related historical packages construct partial_swap.shared.SharedPointCircuit before verify. A faster identical constructor does not change kappa or the binding complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship an equivalence-preserving partial_swap SharedPointCircuit.__init__ change with frozen baseline on the #2039 tip, identical structure and receipts on the historical h=46 circuit, pin-only certificate refresh, registered replay and a measured before/after median. Do not reopen verify digests, ExclusionCircuit/DisjointTensor support masks (#2001), or edit scripts/shared_point_circuit.py.
evidence: PASS_PARTIAL_SWAP_INIT via research/partial-swap-init/verify.py (also under -O); PASS_IDENTICAL_PARTIAL_SWAP_INIT_RECEIPTS via benchmark.py; certificates/partial-swap-network.json changes only scripts/partial_swap/shared.py in source_sha256 relative to the #2039 tip pin.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for orientation, overlap search, profiling, implementation, packaging, benchmarking and writing. Not independent human peer review.

open_questions.question: Should research packages that pin live scripts/partial_swap/shared.py bytes (for example copied-fixed / skip-strip provenance) refresh that one SHA-256 entry after this equivalence-preserving constructor rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those provenance packages bind working-tree bytes of shared.py; leaving old pins keeps this tooling PR focused, but a later full provenance replay on main would see a hash mismatch until refreshed.
open_questions.first_step: Open a dedicated provenance follow-up that only rewrites the shared.py entry after confirming circuit_sha256 identity.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pin repair outside certificates/partial-swap-network.json is outside this tooling change.

open_questions.question: Once open #2039 and #2054 land, should main's partial_swap and canonical constructors share a single tested helper for the merge/lookup loop?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The two producers deliberately diverge on point_order / pair_ids sorting and inlined local support checks; a shared helper risks coupling those contracts, but duplicated micro-opts drift.
open_questions.first_step: Diff the two optimized __init__ bodies after both land and decide whether a private helper preserves both historical contracts.
open_questions.blocked_by: Depends on merge order of #2039 / #2054 / this follow-up.
